subject: Post-demo: MAP draft, technical gaps & milestone asks
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + MAP draft (technical milestone asks)

Hi Julie — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we all have alignment. I’ve attached a first-pass MAP draft (MAP_draft_HealthGrid_v1.pdf) and a small sample dataset you mentioned for early benchmarks.

What we covered (short):
- Goal: validate latency/cost envelope for clinical summarization use-case and confirm security artifacts for procurement.
- Next big milestone: technical evaluation (benchmarks) to be completed before PO/contract signature.

Proposed technical milestone asks (please confirm):
1) Baseline benchmark run (Redwood-provided container) on sample dataset — target p90 latency <= 350ms / token at 2048 context, cost target <= $0.0008/token.
2) Model shortlist evaluation: 3 candidate open models + 1 Redwood-verified small-quant model.
3) End-to-end integration smoke test (API + VPC egress) with 1 week of traffic profiling.

Owners we proposed in the MAP:
- Redwood: Tech lead (Karthik) for benchmark execution + results write-up; Solutions (Marissa) for integration orchestration; Ben for MAP tracking and commercial sync.
- HealthGrid: Eng owner (Julie) for infra access and dataset validation; Procurement for SOW/PO timeline.

Target close: end of July 2027 (we penciled 2027-07-30) assuming benchmarks meet acceptance criteria and procurement sigs.

Open dependencies we flagged:
- HealthGrid to provide sanitized sample dataset and any throttling constraints.
- Network/VPC egress IP allowlist for the smoke test.
- Clear acceptance criteria for quality/regression (we suggested a small prompt set).

Please see attached MAP draft for milestone timeline. Would you and your Eng owner be able to confirm infra access and dataset by end of week?

Thanks — Ben

Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
Attachments: MAP_draft_HealthGrid_v1.pdf (pdf), sample-inference-dataset.csv (csv stub)

From: Julie Park <julie@healthgrid.com>

Cc: Eng <eng@healthgrid.com>, Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + MAP draft (technical milestone asks)

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear recap. We’re aligned on the high-level milestones and the proposed target close (end of July) looks reasonable from a commercial standpoint.

Quick answers:
- I’ll own providing the sanitized sample dataset. Expect a first drop (500 rows) by Wed EOD, full sample by next Monday.
- Eng will coordinate network allowlisting; I’ve looped them in.
- Procurement: we need to run the SOW through legal — I’m attaching our SOW template so your legal team can pre-populate standard fields.

Two constraints to call out:
1) For any PII/PHI processing we prefer a dedicated VPC or strict IP egress controls (we’re not comfortable with shared-hosted inference without an explicit SLA).
2) Our evaluation window is tight — we need the benchmark results in two weeks to keep the July close.

I’ve attached SOW-template-HealthGrid.docx and will send the sample dataset as an encrypted attachment (or via secure link) when ready.

Thanks — Julie

Julie Park | Director, Product — HealthGrid
julie@healthgrid.com
Attachments: SOW-template-HealthGrid.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Julie Park <julie@healthgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap + MAP draft (technical milestone asks) — technical execution plan

Team — forwarding Julie’s confirmations. Karthik, can you confirm the execution plan below and call out specific infra/credentials we need from HealthGrid? Key asks from Julie: sanitized dataset by Wed (500 rows) and network allowlist.

Proposed execution plan (high level):
- Day 0–1: receive dataset + allowlist entries. Validate format and tokenization; sanity checks.
- Day 2–6: run baseline slate (3 models + 1 quantized) at the 2048 context length target across 1000 inputs; capture p50/p90 latency, tokens-per-second, and per-token cost estimate.
- Day 7: write-up and signal for integration smoke test scheduling.

Acceptance criteria (suggested):
- Latency: p90 <= 350ms at typical batch sizes (we’ll propose exact batch config after seeing input size distribution).
- Cost: estimate at <= $0.0008/token for the chosen model variant under production batching.
- Quality: no more than 12% drop vs reference on the diagnostic prompt set (will define set with HealthGrid).

Attachments we’ll push to the shared Drive: benchmark-specs.md, runbook, and result template. Any other items to add?

— Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Julie Park <julie@healthgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + MAP draft (technical milestone asks) — benchmark specifics

Thanks — short answer: yes, plan looks good. A few technical clarifications and asks so we don’t hit surprises during the run.

1) Exact benchmark spec (we’ll add to benchmark-specs.md):
   - Sample size: 1,000 clinical notes (500 short, 300 medium, 200 long).
   - Context window: up to 2048 tokens, measured at 128-token increments for perf curves.
   - Metrics: p50/p90 latency per token, memory (peak GPU memory/use), throughput (tokens/sec), and cost estimate normalized to our hosted pricing math.

2) Model shortlist (recommended):
   - Model A: ClinicalT5-3B (open) — baseline for quality.
   - Model B: MedOmega-2.7B (open) — strong summary coherence.
   - Model C: LLaMA2-7B (quant) — cheap/fast candidate.
   - Redwood-quant-4bit-optimized (internal-variant) — experimental but likely best cost profile.

3) Environment/credentials we’ll need from HealthGrid:
   - Allowlist of egress IPs (we’ll provide our runcluster IP block).
   - Short-lived API key scoped to the trial endpoints or a VPC peering token (preferred).
   - A sanitized sample dataset as agreed (CSV + metadata describing fields).

4) Acceptance criteria detail:
   - Latency: p90 <= 350ms at evaluation batch size 8 for short/medium examples; for long examples we’ll target p90 <= 650ms.
   - Cost: per-token estimate <= $0.0008 for the final model variant under realistic batching; include cost sensitivity at 2x and 5x QPS.
   - Quality: we will provide a 25-prompt diagnostic set; success = >=88% pass-rate on rubric items (factuality, completeness).

I’ll drop benchmark-specs.md to the Drive and plan to kick the baseline run as soon as we have the dataset and allowlist. We should also schedule a 30-min sync after results (tentative date: 2027-07-05).

Karthik

Karthik Iyer | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
